name: Anarchism without adjectives
summary: A pluralist current in anarchism that treats abolition of the state and of imposed authority as the shared core and treats economic schemes (mutualism, collectivism, communism, individualism) as secondary matters to be tried freely. It opposes sectarian disputes among anarchist schools and rejects fixed blueprints for the future society.
scope: The late 19th and early 20th century tendency named by Fernando Tarrida del Mármol in 1889 and shared by Ricardo Mella, Voltairine de Cleyre and, in organization, Errico Malatesta. Answers rest on their texts. Where they are silent, answers are inferred from general anarchist opposition to authority and are low confidence. Excludes anarcho-capitalism and the separate schools it tolerates only as options.

keyFigures.name: Fernando Tarrida del Mármol
keyFigures.role: Coined the phrase in 1889 and argued economic disputes should not divide anarchists.

keyFigures.name: Voltairine de Cleyre
keyFigures.role: Adopted the term and argued anarchism is compatible with mutualism through communism.

keyFigures.name: Errico Malatesta
keyFigures.role: Urged a single plural organization of anarchists of different schools.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Anarchists want care provided through mutual aid and voluntary cooperatives, not state programs; universal access is welcome but the state as provider is not, and the pluralist strand leaves the means open.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A statutory wage floor presumes the state and wage labor; adherents would prefer direct action by workers to win pay, so they tend to see it as a reform that legitimizes the system.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The strand refuses to fix an economic system, accepting mutualist markets and communist distribution alike, so adherents split; the statement's contrast with government is also not a clean anarchist question.

public-ownership.rationale: Anarchists reject state ownership as concentrated power; they would favor common or cooperative control by the people involved, which the statement's word publicly does not mean.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation is a state power adherents reject on principle, though they want wealth redistributed; most would prefer expropriation or abolition of privilege over higher state taxes.

unions-good.rationale: De Cleyre treats trade unions as the base of cooperative workers' groups, and Malatesta urged anarchists to work within labor organization.

property-fundamental.rationale: Malatesta holds private property is the root of economic privilege that government defends, and de Cleyre wanted natural resources free to all; the pluralist strand still tolerates individualist possession by use.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anarchists want corporate power ended or dissolved by social action, not regulated by the state, which they see as its ally; a regulation answer would be inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents oppose state welfare as an institution but not help for the poor; they hold that common property and mutual aid, not cutting support, are the remedy, so they would not endorse the dependency claim.

worker-ownership.rationale: De Cleyre names mutualist and communist cooperation as options for workers' own production, and Malatesta wants the means of production in common; the strand tolerates other forms, so not strongly.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anarchists reject state power as illegitimate and surveillance as a tool of domination, with no exception recorded for security justifications.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The harm of prohibition and the principle against compulsion lead anarchists to oppose drug laws; the sources do not discuss drugs, so this is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: De Cleyre writes that if no laws are made on speech, speech will be free; adherents oppose legal restrictions while answering hatred by social means.

strong-leader.rationale: Tarrida describes anarchists as enemies of all authority and imposition, which excludes a leader empowered to bypass others.

state-harmful.rationale: De Cleyre states the anarchist conclusion as no government whatsoever, and Tarrida and Malatesta give the abolition of the state as the common ground of the strand.

limit-guns.rationale: Adherents oppose state disarmament of the people and favor voluntary armed force, though they have no uniform pro-gun doctrine; inferred from de Cleyre's preference for voluntary arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Malatesta argues police and judges mainly protect privilege, and anarchists reject standing professional force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Liberty over personal conduct implies no legal ban, but the sources do not address the question and some anarchists see it as exploitation under wage labor.

decide-locally.rationale: Malatesta wants organization built from the bottom up through free local agreement and de Cleyre pictures small freely cooperating communes, though federation beyond locality is also accepted.

rehabilitation.rationale: Malatesta rejects vengeful punishment and favors treating and redeeming offenders, so prisons as punishment are unwelcome.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchists hold no authority is sacred, including family hierarchy, though the strand takes no uniform line and tolerates voluntary traditional choices.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anarchists oppose state control of relationships, so state-licensed marriage in either form is not their cause; legality as a question is largely indifferent to them.

abortion-legal.rationale: Self-ownership and opposition to state compulsion point to choice, but the founding texts do not discuss it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Malatesta criticizes priests as propagators of falsehood upholding power, and de Cleyre traces the state to religious development; adherents reject enlarged religious public authority but accept private belief.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anarchists oppose domination and racial hierarchy but reject state-led remedies, and the strand leaves the means open so adherents are split on the statement as framed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anarcha-feminism treats gender hierarchy as a social domination, but the strand's founding texts do not address it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and national loyalty as authority, though they have no hostility to local customs as such.

gradual-change.rationale: Malatesta supports revolutionary action to dispossess owners, and the strand rejects deference to established institutions, though it emphasizes experiment over blueprints.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anarchists reject borders as state coercion and would not accept state restriction of movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anarchists reject government at any level, so a stronger international authority is a larger state.

free-trade.rationale: Mutualist markets and communist distribution are both accepted by the strand, and anarchists oppose state tariffs yet reject capitalist competition, so adherents split.

nation-first.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and the state's claim on loyalty, preferring cooperation across borders.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents oppose state armies and war but sympathize with victims; most would reject state military intervention while backing popular solidarity.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are state coercion, so anarchists accept their abolition as part of ending the state; the stated primary sources do not discuss it, hence medium.

limit-growth.rationale: The founding texts predate environmental debate and the strand takes no side; social ecologists and primitivists differ from communist and mutualist adherents.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Adherents care about ecology but reject government action as the means, so they are split between voluntary social action and doubt over state remedies.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The strand takes no stand on technology; anarchists range from Kropotkin's optimism to anarcho-primitivist skepticism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nothing in the strand addresses nuclear power; adherents split between ecological opposition and technological optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Malatesta supports revolutionary action to dispossess owners, and de Cleyre lets each person choose methods including insurrection.

experts-over-public.rationale: Malatesta doubts rule by the best people and says organization should flow from the free agreement of those affected.

central-planning.rationale: Malatesta and Tarrida reject blueprints and authority imposed from above, and de Cleyre sees compulsory regulation as the danger of joint administration.

socialized-markets.rationale: De Cleyre accepts mutualist cooperation among workers, and the strand tolerates markets so long as no one imposes a system, so the statement fits as one permitted form.

land-value-tax.rationale: De Cleyre wants natural resources free to all and anarchists reject taxation by the state; a single tax is a state remedy few adherents would back.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Anarchists want inherited privilege ended through abolition of private property, not through state taxation, so they would not endorse the tax as the remedy.

basic-income.rationale: A state-paid income keeps the state in place; adherents would prefer distribution through common property or mutual aid.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs are state economic coercion and aligned with the nation, both of which anarchists reject.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Malatesta and Tarrida reject imposed economic direction, and anarchists oppose state control of the economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Individualists and mutualists in the strand favor small holdings, but communists reject property, and the strand accepts both; adherents split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communist anarchists want money and wages gone, mutualists and individualists keep exchange; the strand explicitly leaves this choice to each community.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The strand opposes state institutions, so central banks go; the clause leaving money to the market is only one accepted option, so this is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices is state authority over labor, which anarchists reject.

one-party-rule.rationale: Tarrida calls anarchists enemies of all authority and imposition, which excludes any party leading the state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: De Cleyre states the anarchist position as no government whatsoever, which rules out monarchs as much as other rulers.

democracy-best.rationale: Malatesta doubts that elections and majorities produce good outcomes, and de Cleyre calls majority rule unworkable, though adherents prefer voluntary consensus to hierarchy.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists prefer free agreement to ballots, and Malatesta notes majorities can cling to prejudice; direct decision in small assemblies is acceptable but compulsory majority law is not.

workers-councils.rationale: De Cleyre describes workers making their own regulations and trade-union based cooperation, but she does not make councils the political basis, and communes are also envisaged.

right-to-secede.rationale: Her principle of no compulsion means no group may force dissenters to stay in an arrangement, which implies a right of withdrawal.

natural-rulers.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists the enemy of all authority and imposition, rejecting any natural right to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: De Cleyre states that all methods are left to the individual's capacity and decision, and she praised Bresci's act, so adherents do not rule violence out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anarchists reject war as a state and class instrument and the strand shows no glorification of it.

separate-church-state.rationale: De Cleyre roots the state in religious development and wants no government, so any state religion goes, though adherents care more about abolishing both than about separating them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Malatesta treats priests as upholders of power and anarchists oppose law imposed by any authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: De Cleyre says individualism and mutualism resting on property involve a development of the private policeman, which she rejects, though the strand tolerates individualist views.

military-superiority.rationale: Anarchists reject state armies and national rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and ethnic exclusivity as sources of domination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Malatesta frames property and government as a class domination to be overthrown, though the pluralist strand does not adopt a theory of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Communist adherents want distribution by need while individualists and mutualists accept differing outcomes; the strand leaves it open.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Self-governing communities holding land locally fit anarchist principles, but the strand does not address indigenous claims directly.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anarchists oppose colonialism but reject state transfers, and the sources do not address reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Anarchists reject political unions built on state or religious identity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individualist adherents value self-interest while communists stress mutual aid, and the strand accepts both.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Anarchists reject community or state authority over the individual, and de Cleyre defends non-compulsion as the point of agreement.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecological anarchism affirms nature's value, but the founding texts of the strand do not discuss it.

limit-population.rationale: Anarchists reject state compulsion over reproduction, though voluntary birth control has been favored in the movement.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists say yes while communist and mutualist anarchists build on industry, so the strand does not settle this.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No stated position; adherents divide between technological optimism and skepticism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Liberty over one's own body implies freedom to modify it, but the sources do not address the matter.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government by algorithm is still government, and Tarrida's rejection of authority and imposition excludes it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Resistance to state surveillance supports private communication, though the sources do not discuss encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Anarchists seek to overthrow existing hierarchy, not to restore an earlier social order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Tarrida puts anarchism itself as the core and economics as secondary, which gives pragmatic experiment, but adherents still hold firm principles against authority.

direct-action.rationale: De Cleyre treats methods as left to individual choice and anarchists are broadly committed to direct action rather than parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Malatesta's insistence on free agreement and voluntary organization from the start means anarchists generally hold that methods must prefigure the society sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Only the anarcho-primitivist strand holds this and it is outside the without-adjectives mainstream.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Malatesta distinguishes administration from government and accepts delegated tasks, so adherents do not seek an end to specialization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: De Cleyre expresses the vision that all belong to all as each has need and desire, but the strand also accepts mutualist exchange.

production-for-use.rationale: Malatesta ties anarchy to socialism and common property against competition, but the strand tolerates market forms as well.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Malatesta calls private property the root of economic privilege, though individualist adherents in the strand might not accept this wording.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists the enemy of all authority and imposition, which rules out dictatorship by any class.

collective-farming.rationale: Communist anarchists favor collective farming and individualists hold land by use, and de Cleyre accepts the full range, so the strand does not choose.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Malatesta ties government and property to domination, but the strand adopts no theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists hold the state is illegitimate, so its taxes are coercive exactions, though communists put the weight on property rather than tax.

harm-principle.rationale: The strand accepts no compulsion and diverse economic systems, but the statement concerns a state with powers, which adherents reject, so they are split on how to read it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualists in the strand hold rights belong to individuals while communists stress collective freedom, and the strand accepts both.

conscription.rationale: Compulsory service is state coercion and adherents reject armies; de Cleyre prefers only voluntary armed force.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The principle of no compulsion implies freedom to leave, but anarchists reject the state altogether, so neither check is the point.

state-as-business.rationale: The strand rejects the state itself; running it like a business would not make it legitimate.

positive-liberty.rationale: Malatesta treats economic dependence as a form of unfreedom, so material means matter, but the strand does not state this directly.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anarchists focus on state and capital power, not universities and media; the claim is not part of the strand.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The sources do not discuss racial hereditarianism; rejection is inferred from anarchist equality.

organic-representation.rationale: Malatesta rejects delegation of power, and anarchists oppose corporatist representation that would stand in for government.

total-state.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists the enemy of all authority and imposition, the opposite of a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and its national myths, so a nation's radical rebirth is not their program.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anarchists reject state power and conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on oaths of loyalty is the sort of imposition that Tarrida rejects.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor is a direct form of domination and exploitation that anarchists seek to end.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Anarchists see knowledge as shaped by power in places, as Malatesta says of state schooling, but the strand does not claim all knowledge is non-neutral.

universal-morality.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism need not be based on any particular world conception, so adherents are split.

single-common-good.rationale: The strand tolerates plural economic systems and rejects a single imposed blueprint, which cuts against one common good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anarchists reject the creation of states, including national ones, though they support the equal rights of all peoples.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship by state status is a border question adherents reject, though they accept freedom of movement.

revive-national-language.rationale: State imposition of language is a form of authority, though free cultural revival is acceptable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' own cooperation is central to de Cleyre's mutualist and communist options, though the statement's public vote is a state-like element.

school-vouchers.rationale: Malatesta wants education freely organized by parents and teachers rather than government schooling, so state vouchers are an inferior half-measure.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Anarchists do not take a side in state fiscal debates since they oppose the state altogether.

economic-freedom.rationale: De Cleyre wants freedom on a basis of free access to resources, while individualists defend markets and communists reject them, so adherents split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rulers are rejected in principle, though moral example is preferred to force, so the statement is largely rejected on its premise of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anarchists favor self-determination of individuals and communities rather than nation-states.

force-without-un.rationale: Anarchists reject state armies and war regardless of international approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism need not rest on any particular world conception, so this is not required of adherents, though many are rationalists.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anarchists reject citizen status as a state category and oppose excluding people from mutual aid.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The principle of no compulsion argues against forcing work, though communists expect contribution by choice.

class-collaboration.rationale: Malatesta sees property as the root of domination, so partnership between employers and workers is rejected, though the strand does not adopt class war as doctrine.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist-style destruction of institutions is outside the strand; anarchists oppose coercion but have no doctrine on heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Anarchists oppose state blocs, even against western powers, but sympathize with anti-imperial popular movements.

workers-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject national organization in favor of international solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Anarchists reject legal imposition and hierarchy, including roles fixed by law.

ban-interest.rationale: Mutualists hold credit at cost while communists abolish money and individualists tolerate interest; the strand rejects legal bans in any case, so it is split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state and its laws, and racial hierarchy as domination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: De Cleyre and Malatesta see the state as defending owners, but some in the strand see it as having interests of its own, so they differ.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The strand takes no stand, but ecological anarchists oppose expansion, and adherents distrust state-backed industry.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Forced assimilation is coercion by the state or majority, which anarchists reject.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement claim is a conspiracy theory, not part of any anarchist tradition, which rejects nationalism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta doubts elections can produce good leadership, so adherents do not pursue electoral reform.

national-mission.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and its civilizing missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarchist feminists describe patriarchy as structural domination, but the strand's founding texts do not elaborate it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Malatesta treats those who hold power as corrupted by it, so adherents agree that rulers are out of touch.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Compulsory eugenics is state coercion, which anarchists reject, as Malatesta's stress on free agreement shows.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Adherents want police abuses answered but reject state courts, so agreement is partial; inferred from Malatesta's view of police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: De Cleyre rejects the private policeman of property-based systems and states no government whatsoever.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Anarchists oppose racial hierarchy and any state coercion in private life.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anarchism rejects ruling classes and natural authority, which presuppose equal standing, but equality before the law as such is a state concept.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anarchists support revolution across borders but do not run a state to which the doctrine applies.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anarchists regard states as instruments of domination and so tend to agree, though the sources do not address it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Anarchists oppose religious law's coercion and state civil law alike, so neither answer is theirs.

restrict-conversion.rationale: De Cleyre's statement that no law should restrict speech and belief applies; the state has no role in religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Legal bans are state coercion, though adherents may avoid animal use voluntarily.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Malatesta wants schooling free of government control, and adherents oppose state religious instruction, though state schools themselves are rejected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: De Cleyre states the anarchist aim as no government whatsoever, which rejects strengthening a state for any reason.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anarchists say authority is illegitimate even with consent as majority rule, though they favor consent for voluntary associations, so they are split on the framing.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist national economic aims are state goals that adherents reject.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced expulsion of minorities is state coercion that anarchists reject.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Individualist adherents accept this nonaggression principle while others justify revolutionary force, and de Cleyre left methods to individual choice.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's mutual aid answer to this view is central to anarchism, though individualists in the strand accept competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: De Cleyre holds that no laws should restrict speech and assembly, so state bans of parties are rejected.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anarchists hold that dependence on arbitrary power is unfreedom, and De Cleyre ties the private policeman to loss of liberty.

separated-powers.rationale: Anarchists reject all state power rather than dividing it, though checks are preferable to unchecked rule.

vanguard-party.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists enemies of all authority and imposition, which excludes a disciplined party leading the workers.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Malatesta ties anarchy to socialism against privilege, and the strand's communists stress need, though law and institutions as agents is not an anarchist framing.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Adherents prefer common tenure or occupancy but support tenants' security; the policy is not an anarchist cause.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Anarchists treat strikes as workers' direct action and oppose laws restricting them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malatesta attributes poverty to property and government rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Anarchists reject the claim as nationalist, and favor free association among diverse people.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: De Cleyre proposes a free jury chosen by lot, but anarchists reject public office as such, so adherents are split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: De Cleyre argues against any laws restricting liberty and calls for resistance to state force in emergencies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State price fixing is an imposed regulation that adherents reject, though they want essentials to be accessible by other means.

party-controls-media.rationale: De Cleyre states that no laws should concern speech so that it is free, which rules out ruling-party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Tarrida rejects all authority and imposition, so no ruling party can command an army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship is a state construct and adherents oppose barriers to movement and membership.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Malatesta rejects delegation of power, so representatives are not wanted, but pay equality would be preferred if any existed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Tarrida describes anarchist groups where there is no authority and roles are only practical, which cuts against binding discipline, though Malatesta wanted a plural organization.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Anarchists reject supranational government as another state, though they accept voluntary federation from below.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists enemies of authority and imposition, which excludes an executive commanding armed forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Malatesta criticizes priests as upholders of power, and anarchists reject hierarchical church authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: De Cleyre states the anarchist aim as no government whatsoever, which excludes rule by religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists see war as a state and class instrument and do not support their own state in it, though pluralist strands were divided over world wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: De Cleyre writes that without laws on speech, speech will be free, which excludes censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Anarchists reject offices of rule altogether, so the question of their duration is a non-issue they would reject.

recall-officials.rationale: Anarchists prefer revocable delegation to permanent rule, though they reject elected office itself.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anarchists reject state military alliances and bases, and support ending them without replacing them with a new bloc.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Individualists and mutualists in the strand hold land by use, but a legal ban on renting is a state measure, so adherents reject it.

people-in-arms.rationale: De Cleyre says the least objectionable armed force is that which springs up voluntarily, which fits popular militias over a standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The strand takes no position; Kropotkin favored a mix of town and country, and others disagree.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Anarchists oppose borders and states and do not take nationalist reunification as a cause.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The claim is a populist one that is not part of anarchist doctrine, though they distrust credentialed authority.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rejecting hierarchies of peoples is consistent with anarchism, though the sources do not discuss it.

death-penalty.rationale: Malatesta rejects vengeful punishment in favor of treatment and redemption, and anarchists reject state killing.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Adherents want education freely organized and not state-run, so the matter is outside the question of state curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Malatesta wants schools outside government control, but anarchists criticize religious falsehood, so they would reject state-mandated creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: De Cleyre states that without laws on speech, speech will be free, so legal restrictions are rejected.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship is a state category that anarchists reject, and descent-based exclusion is hostile to their principles.

minority-language-support.rationale: Anarchists favor free cultural life but not state programs; they would support local autonomy over government support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Anarchists reject general laws burdening anyone, so the exemption is a lesser concern.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: De Cleyre's insistence on non-compulsion and freedom to choose economic and social arrangements extends to social pressure on custom, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anarchists see debt as a tool of economic privilege and favor cancellation, but do not discuss state debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Malatesta ties government to the property it defends, so changing the political order alone leaves domination intact.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Anarchists reject constitutions and governments as such, though an assembly elected to dismantle a regime is less objectionable than one appointed; Malatesta's doubts about elections make agreement limited.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: De Cleyre opposes restrictions on liberty in the name of any state aim.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Adherents support mutual aid across borders but reject state aid, so they split on the statement's wording of a duty of wealthy countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anarchists reject state armies and weapons altogether.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Tarrida's rejection of authority makes a head of state illegitimate whoever elects him.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anarchists oppose central banks as state institutions, whether independent or not, though independence from elected governments is not their concern.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are not anarchist concerns, and adherents oppose historic homeland claims, though not particular peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Adherents hold natural resources should be free to all and communists reject private property, though individualists tolerate possession by use.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anarchists regard the Soviet state as a dominating class power, which supports the state capitalist reading, though the strand does not adopt a specific theory.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The strand takes no position, and anarchists reject state action as the means.

collective-defense.rationale: Anarchists reject state military alliances, though they accept voluntary mutual defense among communities.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anarchists oppose conquest and imposed rule, though they reject all state claims to territory.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anarchists oppose church power as Malatesta does but reject state power over it too.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Tarrida's rejection of all authority applies to any head of state, symbolic or not.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: De Cleyre's principle of no compulsion implies no coercion of a region that wants to leave.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Anarchists reject the larger state but accept regions keeping their own arrangements, so the framing is mixed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: De Cleyre states the aim of no government whatsoever, and traces the state to religious development she rejects.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Anarchists reject taxation, and a flat tax favors the wealthy against their egalitarian aims.

character-from-environment.rationale: Anarchists since Kropotkin emphasize that social conditions shape character, though the founding texts here do not state it directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Authority beyond limits is the imposition Tarrida rejects, though anarchists also reject law as state power.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Anarchists reject constitutions as devices of rule rather than seeking the best mix of rulers.

leader-cult.rationale: Tarrida makes anarchists the enemy of all authority, which excludes veneration of a national leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anarchists reject court authority and the sources say nothing on custody, so the question does not fit.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anarchists doubt the state socialist premise, though they agree party leaders may restore domination.

land-redistribution.rationale: De Cleyre sympathizes with land becoming the free communal possession of those who work it, though the state redistribution mechanism is not favored.

refugee-return.rationale: Anarchists support free movement and oppose expulsions, but they do not discuss descendants' return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Anarchists reject state territorial claims on ethnic grounds.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: De Cleyre holds that no laws restricting belief and speech are legitimate, so punishing apostasy is excluded.

women-must-cover.rationale: De Cleyre rejects state laws on personal liberty and speech, and no authority may compel dress.

common-currency.rationale: Anarchists reject state money and so are split between voluntary exchange systems and abolition.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Anarchists reject political unions built on ancestry as nationalism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Anarchists favor self-governing communities but not state-recognized minority bodies, so they are split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Anarchists oppose states and national homelands but support equal liberty for all where they live, so they are split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism need not rest on a particular world conception, so adherents do not share a theory of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anarchists want concentrated economic power dissolved but not through the state, which they see as its ally.

no-bailouts.rationale: Malatesta sees government as the defender of owners, so bailouts of owners with public money are opposed, though adherents regard the question as secondary.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Malatesta warns majorities cling to prejudice and anarchists reject state courts altogether.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Adherents want equality but reject mandated state bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are state projects, which anarchists reject.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding agreements between states are state action, so adherents lean against them.

moral-incentives.rationale: Communist adherents expect contribution by choice and mutualists use exchange, so the strand leaves incentives open.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: De Cleyre left methods to individual choice and praised acts like Bresci's, but Malatesta stressed mass action, so adherents split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Malatesta attacks economic privilege and government as defender of it, and anarchists reject inherited rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Education should be free of state and national control, so a nationally centered history curriculum is not wanted.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anarchists reject rule over others and colonialism.

patriotic-education.rationale: De Cleyre criticizes state schools for teaching deference to government and wants instruction never entrusted to any government.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anarchists reject state preference schemes but oppose racial discrimination, so they are split.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money creation preserves state power, though mutualists favor mutual credit, so adherents split but lean against a public body.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Anarchists predicted collapse in places but the strand holds no doctrine of crisis.

delink-world-market.rationale: The strand takes no position on development strategy and adherents split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist category that the strand has not adopted.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Individualists accept free association even where unpleasant, while anarchists oppose the domination discrimination expresses, so adherents split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: De Cleyre argues written guarantees fail unless people defend them, so adherents give constitutions little weight.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anarchists reject colonial rule and state treaties imposed on peoples, though the sources do not discuss them.

elective-rulers.rationale: Malatesta doubts elections can produce good rulers and anarchists reject rule altogether, so election is a lesser evil at best.

minority-veto.rationale: De Cleyre's point of agreement is no compulsion, so no group may bind a dissenter without consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: De Cleyre endorses popular resistance and a little rebellion now and then against rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Malatesta rejects government by elections and parliaments.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Anarchists extend opposition to domination to animals in some strands, but the founding texts do not discuss it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents are split between those favoring vegetarianism and those accepting use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Anarchists want inequality and privilege ended, not softened by the duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: De Cleyre wants people strictly minding their business but not isolating themselves, and anarchists engage in direct action though they avoid parliamentary politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Some anarchists share this view but the strand has no stated position.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Malatesta sees force and priests both sustaining power, but the strand does not adopt a hegemony theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: No stated position of the strand.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anarchists reject public office and citizenship distinctions.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties and does not apply to anarchists.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No stated position; adherents favor mutual aid and local autonomy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Anarchists reject state territorial claims and war to recover land.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anarchists reject any group's political rule over another, so leadership by descent is not accepted.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anarchists oppose fascism but reject constitutional founding of any state, so they are split on the framing.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anarchists condemn both as state domination but would not equate them without reservation.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anarchists reject this revisionism, though the sources do not discuss the war.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents do not defend statues of rulers and see them as state symbols.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Anarchists reject Western state institutions but do not treat other civilizations' states as better.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anarchists reject armies and their political roles.

paid-care-work.rationale: Communist anarchists reject wages while others accept recognition, so they split.

filial-duty.rationale: Anarchists reject duties imposed by authority, though they accept voluntary care.

office-by-exam.rationale: Anarchists reject public offices and the state's bureaucracy.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Anarchists reject state control of ownership and the national framing, though they dislike corporate power, so blocking by the state is not their remedy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The principle of no compulsion implies freedom to leave a marriage, though anarchists oppose state marriage itself.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Malatesta favors delegation of tasks rather than power, so delegates would be removable and bound.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Adherents prefer mutual aid, and private companies managing savings fits individualist markets only partly.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Individualists hold land by use and communists hold it in common, and neither wants national ownership, so the strand splits on the statement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Anarchists reject government and its budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: De Cleyre opposes state compulsion in education and public life.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Anarchists reject state restrictions on property by nationality.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The strand has no position on legal doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Communist and ecological anarchists criticize consumerism, but the strand has no stated position.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State arming of insurgents is state power politics, which anarchists reject.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power invasion of allied states is imperial coercion that anarchists reject.

corporate-influence.rationale: Malatesta sees government as defender of owners, so anarchists agree that property holders hold too much influence over it.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: De Cleyre opposes state restrictions on speech and association.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local authorities are still governments, so adherents lean against, though local control is preferred over national.

job-guarantee.rationale: The state as employer of last resort retains wage labor and the state, so adherents lean against.

democratic-peace.rationale: Anarchists reject spreading democracy by states, as Malatesta doubts parliaments, and the claim is not theirs.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The SEP presents the core anarchist claim that no political authority is legitimate, so there is no general duty to obey law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarchists reject state intervention but support popular solidarity across borders, so the statement's sweep is mixed.

industrial-unions.rationale: De Cleyre treats trade unions as the base of cooperative groups, though the strand has no fixed view on industrial versus craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The conspiracy claim is an antisemitic or racist trope that anarchism does not hold.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The principle of no compulsion and opposition to state licensing implies marriage needs no legal status, though not stated directly.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Anarchists distrust state secrecy but reject a legal right framework, so they are split on wording.

local-production.rationale: Kropotkin favored local production, but mutualists accept trade, so the strand has no fixed view.

informal-organisation.rationale: Malatesta wanted a single plural organization while Galleanisti rejected formal organization, so the strand is split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Anarchists reject both national and international law as state authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject national communities defined by religion and state.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchists reject tribute and hierarchy between states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Anarchists reject tax and revenue by governments, so they are split on the statement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anarchist communists distinguish personal belongings from the means of production, and Malatesta wants common property in the latter, though individualists hold more.

defeat-communism.rationale: Tarrida wanted libertarian communists tolerated in anarchism and anarchists oppose state communism by other means, so adherents would reject war against communism as such.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The strand takes no stand on state-funded systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism need not rest on a particular world conception, so adherents hold varied religious views.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anarchists see capitalism as privilege but the strand holds no stated theory of stages.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Malatesta ties domination to property and government, which supports linking equality to economic change, though the sources do not discuss women directly.

socialized-care.rationale: Anarchists favor communal provision but not state services, so they split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language policing by the state is coercion that anarchists reject.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anarchists reject state treaties, but they accept communities' agreements, so they are split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: De Cleyre describes small independent freely cooperating communes as one communist option, but the strand accepts other forms.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-driven settlement to change ethnic composition is coercion that anarchists reject.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchist communists reject the statement's rejection of communism while mutualists and individualists agree, and the strand tolerates both.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchists reject state or national claims to land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: It is a falsification of history that anarchists do not accept.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: De Cleyre rejects laws against personal liberty, so criminalizing private sexual relations is excluded.

suppress-opposition.rationale: De Cleyre says no laws should concern speech and assembly, which excludes suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: De Cleyre says no laws on speech so that speech is free, which excludes blasphemy law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anarchists reject colonial rule and exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The religious obligation belongs to Islamic doctrine and anarchism does not hold it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Anarchists reject religious rule and want all rulers removed, not replaced by theocracy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Malatesta wants organization built from the bottom up through free local agreement, which fits direct participation, though anarchists reject democracy's compulsion.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anarchists oppose all domination together, but the founding texts do not use this framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anarchists oppose state classification of identity, so recognition by law is not their frame.

assisted-dying.rationale: Self-determination implies freedom over one's death but the sources do not discuss it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anarchists reject the parliamentary spectrum but mostly place themselves on the left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Malatesta criticizes wage dependence on owners, which anarchists generally share, but the term belongs to Marx.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The claim is hostile to a religion that anarchists treat as a matter of individual belief.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: De Cleyre traces the state to religious development and rejects government, including authority from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anarchists reject state coercion on dress and reject state institutions, so the statement's framing is not theirs.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The question is about legal doctrine and adherents rely on direct action.

social-market-economy.rationale: Anarchists reject state regulation and the statement's rule-setting, though a pluralist strand accepts market mutualism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anarchists reject standing armies and state armed force, though they accept voluntary popular defense.

rich-first.rationale: Malatesta opposes economic privilege, and the strand favors equal conditions, so letting some grow rich first is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anarchists oppose state blocs and would stay out of them, though as a state policy it is not their frame.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Tarrida rejects authority and imposition, so hereditary succession of any ruler is excluded.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: De Cleyre names mutualism among the systems that free communities may choose, and mutual credit is its distinctive institution, though the strand does not require it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anarchists see lenders and states as allied defenders of owners, so they favor refusal.

property-franchise.rationale: Tarrida rejects authority and imposition, and anarchists reject voting limits that privilege property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The SEP describes ecological and feminist anarchism linking domination of nature and women, though the strand's founding texts do not.

reification.rationale: The term belongs to Marxist theory not adopted in the strand.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: De Cleyre criticizes commerce for pushing government toward tyranny and shows property's power over liberty, so agreement is likely though not stated for the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Malatesta rejects penal codes and legislators as serving the privileged, so adherents reject law-making rulers altogether.

racial-franchise.rationale: Tarrida rejects authority and imposition, which excludes voting restricted by race.

online-participation.rationale: The sources do not discuss it and anarchists reject voting as the means.

open-government-data.rationale: Anarchists distrust the state and favor transparency but reject the framework.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: De Cleyre rejects laws against personal liberty, which excludes restrictions on marriage by religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anarchists favor direct economic action but oppose discriminatory targeting of minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: De Cleyre proposes a free jury by lot and anarchists favor deliberation, but state-convened assemblies are still governmental.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Anarchists treat religion as a private matter and reject authoritative doctrine, so the statement does not fit.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: De Cleyre sees commerce and property pushing government toward tyranny, which supports that concentrated wealth endangers liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anarchists reject armies, so the statement does not apply, though they reject discrimination.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Anarchists reject state teaching of any creed, though Malatesta criticizes priests.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Malatesta argues police and judges mainly protect privilege and wants offenders treated, so adherents favor replacing them, though he allows defense against anti-social acts.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Anarchists reject executive power and favor local self-rule, which does not align with power sharing at the top.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Malatesta cites voluntary associations like the Red Cross as examples of organization without government, but charity as an answer to poverty is not accepted by adherents who want to end property.

term-limits.rationale: Anarchists reject offices, though rotation is preferred to permanence if any exist.

vote-delegation.rationale: Malatesta rejects delegation of power, so adherents are split on liquid delegation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Anarchists reject religious hierarchy and so do not address who staffs it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy in marriage, though they would prefer no authority at all.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Anarchists oppose citizenship barriers, though they reject voting as the means.

rent-control.rationale: State price caps are regulation that anarchists reject, though they oppose landlordism.

abolish-ip.rationale: Tucker's individualists split on patents and copyright while communist and mutualist adherents oppose monopolies, so the strand is divided.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements are a state training device that anarchists reject.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anarchists reject state armaments and hosting such weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anarchists reject state military machinery and foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anarchists reject state acts, but support the truth being acknowledged.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Malatesta calls private property the root of privilege, and mutualists and communists oppose income from ownership alone, though individualists accept rent in places.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Malatesta accepts defensive force against anti-social acts, so absolute pacifism is not the strand's view.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Anarchists reject national myth and the continuity story supporting the state.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anarchist theory does not take a stand.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The strand takes no position on feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Anarchists honor their own martyrs but not those who die for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism need not rest on any world conception, which excludes making politics a spiritual war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anarchists reject national homelands but accept cultural ties, so they split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Anarchists reject state building but not cultural renewal, so they split on the framing.

god-not-male.rationale: The strand does not address theology.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The strand does not address theology.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Anarchists reject ethnic ownership policies as coercion and hierarchy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anarchists reject administrative units of rule though they accept self-governing communities.

independent-unions.rationale: De Cleyre sees workers' organizations as free, voluntary federations, which excludes state or party control of unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Malatesta ties anarchy to socialism, though anarchists want no political power for any class.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Anarchists want such goods held in common but not by local government, so they split on the wording.

municipal-property.rationale: Communist anarchists favour communal ownership while individualists and mutualists differ, so the strand tolerates this rather than requiring it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Malatesta wants organization from the bottom up by free agreement with delegation of tasks and not power, matching a confederation of coordinating delegates.

family-wage.rationale: Anarchists reject wage labor in communism but mutualists accept wages, and the strand has no position.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The strand takes no position on regulation.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Resistance to state monitoring supports untraceable exchange, though the sources do not discuss it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anarchists favor freedom from state identification, though the sources do not discuss it.

person-over-state.rationale: De Cleyre treats the individual's freedom from state coercion as central, though communists put the community in a mutual role.

spiritual-nature.rationale: De Cleyre says anarchism needs no particular world conception, so adherents hold varied views.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Anarchists reject a national legislature's authority over regions.

dense-cities.rationale: No stated position; Kropotkin favored integration of town and country.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anarchists reject racial identity politics as a basis for organizing rule.

racial-pride.rationale: The strand does not address it, and adherents differ on identity pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anarchists reject state wars, including defensive ones as a state function, though they accept popular defense.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation as a political unit.

communal-electorates.rationale: Anarchists reject electoral representation and communal political divisions.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The claim is a nationalist conspiracy view that anarchists do not hold.

free-public-college.rationale: Anarchists want education freely organized and not state-run, so the statement's public provision is not their form.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Taxes are state tools that adherents reject, though they accept the aim.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological anarchists agree, though the founding texts do not discuss it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The strand takes no position and some anarcha-feminists reject the claim.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anarchists want armies abolished, so lower armaments is a step in that direction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists reject state secrecy and support open dealing among peoples, though they reject diplomacy among governments.

capital-controls.rationale: State control of capital movement is state economic power that adherents reject.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Tarrida del Mármol's founding call for anarchism without adjectives leaves the economic form of a free society to experiment by free groups, and Mella urged the same tolerance; this is the strand's defining claim.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: De Cleyre rejects government altogether and favours voluntary armed association; a state monopoly on force is what anarchists want abolished.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Anarchism is antimilitarist, rejecting state armies and wars between states; refusal by individuals follows from rejecting imposed authority.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: the tendency tolerates syndicalist and collectivist schemes, where workers act as a group, but individualists within it would not require unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose state redistribution through taxation and want the wage system itself replaced, though they would welcome higher incomes.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: legal limits are coercive rules enforced by the state; anarchists want no state to borrow or to be bound, and the pluralist strand takes no position.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose exploitation between nations but want to abolish states rather than rewrite their rules, and the strand is silent on it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Abolition of the state is the shared core; Malatesta and De Cleyre want government dismantled and replaced by voluntary organisation, not captured.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: pricing nature fits market schemes that the tendency treats as one option among many, but anarchist ecology generally rejects commodifying nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and patriotic loyalty as impositions on free individuals.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: anarchists see debt as a tool of domination and would welcome relief, though not necessarily through the state.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose central domination and exploitation of the many by privileged centres, so the framing fits their general analysis.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the strand rests on a shared capacity for free cooperation and mutual aid, but says nothing about not redesigning human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose state funding and control of institutions, even independent ones, and favour voluntary media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Anarchists oppose religious authority but the strand takes no stand on whether religions share one truth; inferred from general anarchist indifference to doctrine.

farm-price-support.rationale: Anarchists favor voluntary cooperative credit and mutual aid over state guarantees; guaranteed prices need a state, but the pluralist strand tolerates cooperative schemes.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anarchists oppose states and their armaments, so a state keeping nuclear weapons is rejected; inferred from Malatesta's and de Cleyre's opposition to standing armies.

workers-own-party.rationale: Malatesta and de Cleyre reject political parties and parliaments in favor of direct organization; workers should organize in unions and groups instead.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anarchists oppose bodily coercion but also law-making by the state; the strand never addressed the question, so adherents would split between condemning it and rejecting legal prohibition.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The strand supports equality and no authority over women, but also rejects state-defined property and inheritance law; inferred from de Cleyre's feminism.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The strand says nothing about language naming and anarchists have no stake in national language claims; inferred as indifferent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Individualist anarchists favor liability for harm while communist anarchists want collective decisions; the pluralist strand leaves the means open and tolerates both, though both reject agency regulation by the state.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Anarchists reject any official role in making law for hereditary or customary rulers, since they reject all government; inferred from de Cleyre's 'no government whatsoever'.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anarchists give priority to freedom and voluntary agreement and did not frame the environment as overriding it; ecological concern comes later in the tradition.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Malatesta rejects fixed punishments and the legal machinery of government, favoring free settlement of wrongs without the state's law.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anarchists oppose state-imposed requirements and border controls; inferred from the rejection of compulsion by authority.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the principle of voluntary association; Tarrida del Marmol leaves economic arrangements open but opposes compulsion.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from de Cleyre's rejection of state authority over individuals; anarchists reject voting as a state control and the issue is not addressed directly.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Anarchists oppose any state authority over belief, so the state would give no interpretation of a religion legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Malatesta holds that government by the majority is still government; anarchism seeks to abolish rulers rather than choose them by election.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of imposed authority over personal life; de Cleyre wrote against marriage as a compulsory institution.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anarchism opposes state coercion over individuals, so state shutdowns of communication are rejected, though the issue is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: anarchists oppose state welfare in favor of mutual aid and cooperatives, and a state-run cash scheme would still rely on the state.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from de Cleyre's work on women's liberation; anarchists reject the state's vote but oppose limiting any group's rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not directly addressed; de Cleyre criticized church-sanctioned marriage but the pluralist current takes no common position on religion as the main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the anarchist rejection of hierarchy and imposed categories; the sources do not discuss race directly.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to state apparatus; anarchists would pursue equality without new state agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Individualist strands accept occupancy and use, but communist and collectivist strands reject first-come ownership; the pluralist strand leans against it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to courts and coercive institutions as state forms.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Anarchists rejected religious authority in the name of free thought.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed directly; de Cleyre and others championed women's freedom, so gender equality is welcome, inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Abolition of the state is the shared core, so defending a ruling state is rejected.

indirect-election.rationale: Anarchists reject offices and rulers; federation by mandated delegates is accepted, but an officeholder chosen indirectly is not the aim.

national-church-status.rationale: Opposition to church and state means no legal privilege for any church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from federalist free association of communities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the principle that people decide their own association.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the view that state borders are arbitrary products of rule.

simple-living.rationale: Many tendencies favour voluntary simplicity, but the pluralist strand leaves it open; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state control of movement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anarchism opposes conscription and the military; the 'or neither' branch applies.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from general anarchist opposition to nation-states; the sources do not discuss it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Malatesta and de Cleyre reject state coercion and punishment without voluntary consent.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anarchists oppose state alignment generally; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of national loyalty and state intervention.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Mutualist, individualist and communist strands diverge on resources; the pluralist stance leaves it open.

self-ownership.rationale: De Cleyre grounds anarchism in individual liberty and self-determination.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the general opposition to state taxation.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Schemes differ by school and pluralists leave them open.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anarchists reject leaders and the state as well as the parties; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: De Cleyre attacks monopoly and legal privilege for the propertied.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the anti-clerical, anti-authority outlook.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that schools differ.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: De Cleyre championed women's freedom, including in marriage, against authority.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from preference for communal control over national state control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Property schemes are left open and anarchists attack both state-backed wealth and enforced equality; the strand treats the economic question as secondary, so it is split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: A tax requires a state to levy it and the strand rejects government; inferred from its general anarchist opposition to authority in s5.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anarchists see racism as one among many forms of domination and a continuing evil; inferred from the general anarchist opposition to authority and imposed hierarchy.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: De Cleyre and Malatesta hold that no law binds the conscientious individual and that justice outranks government decree, which supports disobedience of unjust rules.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anarchists generally welcome machines that cut toil when the gains are shared freely, but the strand gives no programme on work; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Anarchists reject any dominating power and favour many independent communities and federations, but the statement concerns states or civilizations, so the fit is inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Only some of the strands the current tolerates (collectivist, communist) rely on labour-based value, while mutualists and individualists differ; the pluralist stance leaves this open, with a lean against a fixed doctrine.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Anarchists treat patriotism as a tool of rulers and as division among people; De Cleyre and Malatesta reject loyalty to the state.

material-over-identity.rationale: The pluralist current treats economic schemes as secondary, and anarchists also fight authority beyond class, so it is split on priorities.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anarchism rejects the state and any party rule as a matter of definition; Tarrida and Malatesta oppose imposed authority in every form.

missingStatements.text: Anarchists of different economic schools should work together rather than divide over what a free society's economy will look like.
missingStatements.rationale: Tarrida and Mella treat economic debates as secondary and urge tolerance, which defines the strand.

missingStatements.text: No one should draw up a fixed blueprint for the economy of a future free society.
missingStatements.rationale: Malatesta and the strand reject blueprints in favor of free experiment among communities.

missingStatements.text: Different communities should be free to choose different economic systems, from markets to communal sharing.
missingStatements.rationale: De Cleyre states that each group acting in freedom may choose any of the proposed systems.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence because the strand deliberately leaves economic and social questions open. Individualist, mutualist and communist adherents would answer economic statements differently.
